newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway parliament adopts tight 1997 budget.
newsitem.headline: Norway parliament adopts tight 1997 budget.

text.p: The Norwegian parliament on Saturday adopted a tight 1997 national budget in line with a compromise reached a week ago between the Labour minority government and the opposition.
"The Norwegian economy is not overheated and the task now is to prevent it from becoming that," Prime Minister Thorbjoern Jagland told the legislature.
"This is a budget that all the parties can stand up for," he said.
The budget proposal was bound to be passed by parliament after the government and three centrist parties on December 14 agreed how to finance additional spending demanded by the opposition.

Under the compromise, an extra 3.5 billion Norwegian crown ($540 million) will be allocated to local governments for welfare spending than the government planned for in the revised final draft on November 29.
The extra allocations will be covered mainly through a 3.5 percent rise on alcohol, tobacco and petrol taxes, thus leaving the budget balance intact.
The opposition had initially urged the government to take money from the budget surplus, which is expected to swell to 55.4 billion crowns next year thanks to high oil prices.
Norway, a country of 4.3 million people, produces more than three million barrels of oil per day and is the world's second largest crude exporter after Saudi Arabia.

The central bank, commenting on the compromise, noted with satisfaction on Wednesday that the tightening effects of fiscal policy next year will be about the same as the level in the initial draft budget.

The government has said the projected surplus will be put aside in a state petroleum fund to avoid overheating the economy and to secure pensions for future generations the day the offshore oil and gas reserves are depleted.

Anxious not to fuel inflation and keep the economy from overheating, Jagland has avoided the temptation of going on a spending spree in the budget although general elections will be held in September next year.
Jagland, who is also Labour Party chairman, took over the job as prime minister when veteran Labour premier Gro Harlem Brundtland resigned in October. ($1=6.473 Norwegian Crown)
